subject: Math
prompt:
Which of the following ordered pairs $(x, y)$ satisfies the inequality $4x - 2y > 3$?

I. $(2, 1)$
II. $(4, 5)$
III. $(1, 3)$
explanation: Choice C is correct. Substituting $(2, 1)$ into the inequality gives $4(2) - 2(1) > 3$, or $6 > 3$, which is true. Substituting $(4, 5)$ gives $4(4) - 2(5) > 3$, or $6 > 3$, which is true. Substituting $(1, 3)$ gives $4(1) - 2(3) > 3$, or $-2 > 3$, which is false. Therefore, $(2, 1)$ and $(4, 5)$ are the only ordered pairs shown that satisfy the given inequality.
